The value of the $y$-intercept of the parabola shown above  is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(2,2)$ and passes through the point $(-2,-2).$

The general standard equation of an up- or down-opening parabola with vertex at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k),
$$

and substituting $(h,k)=(2,2)$ into the above gives

$$
(x-2)^{2}=4p(y-2).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(-2,-2),$ we substitute $x=-2$ and $y=-2$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2-2)^{2} & =4p(-2-2) \\ 16 & =4p(-4) \\ p & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2} & =-4(y-2).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$ So, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(0-2)^{2} & =-4(y-2) \\ 4 & =-4(y-2) \\ -1 & =y-2 \\ y & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $y$-intercept is $1.$
